title: Vesper and the Inheritance
premise: Estate lawyer Vesper Okonkwo is summoned to probate the will of Marion Voss, a woman who vanished five years ago and was declared legally dead two years later. The will's existence is impossible, and its terms force Vesper to reopen the disappearance everyone in the town of Hallowmere swore was settled. Following entries in Marion's diary that continue past the date she vanished, Vesper uncovers that the town's most respected families staged her death to bury what she knew about a decades-old drowning. In the end, Vesper finds Marion alive in hiding, must choose between exposing the town's complicity or protecting the innocent people entangled in it, and chooses truth, delivering justice for the drowned boy while accepting that he can no longer belong to the town that raised him.
about_author: Casper Ashgrove is the pen name of a former small-town paralegal who spent a decade handling estates in communities where everyone knew everyone's business. Their fiction explores the quiet violence of towns that keep their own ledgers.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Vesper Okonkwo, POV. A courier delivers a sealed will for Marion Voss, dead five years, dated three months after her disappearance. Vesper recognizes the notary stamp as his own firm's, which never handled it. Emotional beat: unease masked as professional calm as he realizes someone wanted him specifically to find this.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The will names Vesper executor and conditions the estate on 'resolving the matter of E. Brandt' within thirty days. He interviews Marion's sister, who insists Marion died by suicide at the quarry. Emotional beat: creeping dread as polite answers reveal a town rehearsed in denial.

chapters.title: Entries Past the End
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV, with diary excerpts. Among Marion's effects he finds her diary; the final entry is dated eleven days after she vanished, describing a boat and a name half-blotted: 'D___'. Emotional beat: vertigo, the ground of the official story giving way beneath him.

chapters.title: The Quarry Committee
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. He pulls old probate files and learns the quarry drowning of Eli Brandt, 1989, was ruled accidental by a coroner who later married into the Hollis family. Three founding families own everything in Hallowmere. Emotional beat: anger hardening into resolve as the pattern emerges.

chapters.title: An Ally With Her Own Reasons
chapters.summary: Alternating Vesper and Deputy Ruth Calloway, POV. Ruth, who worked the original missing-person case and was ordered to close it, comes to Vesper with the search file she was made to falsify. Emotional beat: wary trust between two people who each kept silent too long.

chapters.title: What the Hollis House Keeps
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. At a dinner hosted by patriarch Aldous Hollis, Vesper is offered his dream partnership if he declares the will invalid. That night he finds the diary's missing pages hidden in Marion's law books, naming Aldous's son Daniel at the quarry. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Minus Nine
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. Someone torches the records annex; the diary pages survive only because Vesper took them home. Ruth notices a car following them and traces it to a security firm retained by the Hollis estate. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into urgency, the clock now audible.

chapters.title: The Woman at Larkspur Cabin
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Following a clue in the final diary entry, Vesper drives to a decommissioned lake cabin and finds Marion Voss alive, living under another name, hiding from the men who helped her fake her death after she witnessed Daniel Hollis drown Eli. Emotional beat: shock dissolving into grief for the woman the town erased.

chapters.title: Everything Filed Under Closed
chapters.summary: Vesper and Marion, POV. Marion refuses to testify until Daniel's men corner them at the cabin; Ruth arrives with state police tipped off by Vesper's mailed copies of the evidence. Daniel confesses under arrest; Aldous collapses mid-bribe. Emotional beat: climax, violence breaking open everything the town filed away.

chapters.title: Probate in Daylight
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Months later, Vesper executes the will publicly, funds a memorial for Eli Brandt, and declines the partnership, leaving Hallowmere for good. Marion testifies, rebuilt and unhidden. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution, belonging surrendered for truth, and peace found in finally being seen.
